extracted.intended_audience: small businesses, small organizations, and small government jurisdictions participating in federal rulemaking (notice-and-comment)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for small entities on preparing effective comments under the Regulatory Flexibility Act and related rulemaking processes, including how to identify small-entity status, quantify burdens, demand required analyses, propose less-burdensome alternatives, and seek SBREFA panels. Focused on influencing agency consideration of small business impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory Flexibility Act (RFA) requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The RFA and related laws and executive orders require federal agencies to consider the effects of regulations on small entities; the law allows small firms to engage in regulatory decision-making and directs the Office of Advocacy to monitor agency compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the RFA framework as the legal basis for comments asserting small-entity impacts; cite the RFA and relevant executive orders when arguing that agencies must consider and mitigate burdens on small entities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respond to regulatory flexibility agenda notices
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal agencies endeavor to provide notice of regulatory flexibility agendas to small entities and invite comments upon each subject area on the agenda.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor agencies' regulatory flexibility agendas and submit comments on each relevant subject area listed; timely participation in response to notices is necessary to influence agency consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify Yourself as a Small Entity
rubrics_metrics.description: State your status as a small business, small organization, or small government jurisdiction; provide NAICS code and revenue/employment thresholds; explain how RFA Section 601 categories apply to you.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly label your comment with your small-entity status and supply objective identifiers (NAICS code, revenue/employment figures) so agencies can recognize and quantify the small-entity stake; explicitly map your situation to RFA Section 601 categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantify the Disproportionate Impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate how the proposed rule falls more heavily on small entities by calculating per-employee compliance cost, showing fixed-cost regulatory burden concentration, estimating market exit/concentration effects, and documenting time-to-compliance challenges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide concrete numerical estimates and explanations: compute compliance costs on a per-employee basis, show how fixed costs create disproportionate burdens on small firms, estimate potential firm exits or increased market concentration, and document how long compliance would take for small entities. Use data, examples, and business records where possible to substantiate claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demand RFA-Required Analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Request that agencies prepare the Initial Regulatory Flexibility Analysis (IRFA) for a proposed rule and the Final Regulatory Flexibility Analysis (FRFA) for a final rule; if the agency certifies 'no significant economic impact' for small entities, challenge that certification with data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite the statutory requirement for IRFA/FRFA and explain why the agency's certification is unsupported if applicable; attach or reference data and analysis demonstrating that a full IRFA/FRFA is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggest Regulatory Alternatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose less burdensome approaches, as the RFA requires agencies to consider alternatives such as different compliance/reporting requirements for small entities, differing timetables, performance rather than design standards, and exemptions for small entities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer concrete, practicable alternatives tailored to small entities (e.g., scaled reporting thresholds, delayed compliance deadlines, performance-based standards, explicit exemptions), and explain how each alternative would meet regulatory goals while reducing small-entity burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage SBREFA Panels (Small Business Advocacy Review)
rubrics_metrics.description: For rules under EPA, OSHA, and CFPB, demand a Small Business Advocacy Review (SBAR) panel under SBREFA before publication of a Notice of Proposed Rulemaking (NPRM).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When appropriate, request formation of a SBAR panel early in the rule development process (pre-NPRM) to ensure small-entity concerns are formally considered; reference the agencies (EPA, OSHA, CFPB) and the SBREFA process when asking for a panel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the Office of Advocacy's resources and filings
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office of Advocacy conducts small business outreach, comments in the federal regulatory process, and files comment letters with federal agencies to highlight small business impacts and propose alternatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate with or leverage the Office of Advocacy: seek their outreach, cite their analyses or prior comment letters when supportive, and consider requesting their involvement to amplify small-entity concerns and suggested alternatives.
